name: Incident Response
tagline: Triage a live incident from runbooks, incident history and logs — then propose a fix a human approves before anything is applied.
example_brief: You are on the platform team at Northwind Payments, a fictional payments company. Alerts fire against services like payments-api and webhook-dispatcher, and whoever is on call has about three minutes to work out what is happening, whether it has happened before, what else it is affecting, and what to do about it. You have runbooks, past postmortems, a service catalogue and three live alerts waiting. You will build a triage assistant that does that work end to end — and by Module 4 proposes the fix, with evidence and a rollback plan, for a human to approve before anything is applied.
scenario: You are on the platform team of a payments company. An alert fires at 02:14. The on-call engineer has three minutes to work out what is happening, whether it has happened before, what else it affects, and what to do about it.
best_for: Teams doing SRE, ops, on-call or support engineering — and anyone who needs the human-approval gate to be real rather than theoretical.
difficulty: highest — three different data shapes (documents, a database, log files)
data_you_get: incidents.db — an incident history you query with SQL
log samples from the affected services
a service catalogue with ownership and dependencies

you_will_build.01: A skill that turns an alert into a consistent triage note — same shape every time.
you_will_build.02: Retrieval over runbooks and postmortems, so triage cites the prior incident it resembles.
you_will_build.03: A service dependency graph, so the agent can answer 'what else is affected by this' — which retrieval alone cannot.
you_will_build.04: A remediation proposal carrying evidence, risk and a rollback plan, blocked behind a human approval gate.

final_deliverable: /triage INC-xxxx produces a cited triage note plus a proposed remediation, and cannot apply anything until a human runs /approve.
graph_payoff: Blast radius. 'Which services depend on the component that caused INC-204?' is a multi-hop traversal that similarity search cannot do.
temporal_payoff: Runbooks go stale. The agent must prefer the runbook version that was in force, and say when its guidance was last updated.
